I did not read the _API_TOOL_SETS or _wire_secure_guards definitions.

_wire_secure_guards in lionagi/agent/spec.py (lines 44-56) registers two hook handlers. First, guard_destructive on the "bash" tool via security_pre("bash", guard_destructive). Second, a single guard_paths instance, built as guard_paths(allowed_paths=[workspace_root]), where workspace_root is cwd or Path.cwd(). That same instance is registered via security_pre on the "reader" and "editor" tools. So the path guard is registered on reader and editor, not bash. Note that the function's actual signature is (obj: HooksMixin, cwd: str | None), not (spec: AgentSpec, hooks: dict) as the question states.

_wire_secure_guards (lionagi/agent/spec.py:44) registers two hook handlers, both in the security_pre bucket: (1) guard_destructive on the 'bash' tool (spec.py:52); (2) the guard_paths path guard on the 'reader' and 'editor' tools (spec.py:55-56). Trace of the guard_paths registration: spec.py:50 imports guard_paths from lionagi.agent.hooks; spec.py:53 sets workspace_root = str(Path(cwd) if cwd else Path.cwd()); spec.py:54 builds path_guard = guard_paths(allowed_paths=[workspace_root]) with no denied_paths; spec.py:55 registers path_guard via obj.security_pre('reader', path_guard) and spec.py:56 registers the same instance via obj.security_pre('editor', path_guard). security_pre (spec.py:31-33) appends the handler to hook_handlers['security_pre:<tool_name>']. At call time the _guard closure (hooks.py:99-134) reads args['path'] or args['file_path'], resolves relative paths against the workspace root, and raises PermissionError if the resolved path falls outside it. Sources: lionagi/agent/spec.py and lionagi/agent/hooks.py; verified by reading the source, tests not run.

LIONAGI_HOME defaults to `Path.home() / ".lionagi"` (i.e., `~/.lionagi`) when the LIONAGI_HOME env var is unset. It is defined in `lionagi/_paths.py` line 20: `LIONAGI_HOME: Path = Path(os.environ.get("LIONAGI_HOME", Path.home() / ".lionagi")).expanduser()`.

The MCP config module (`lionagi/mcp/config.py`) imports `LIONAGI_HOME` and `RUNS_ROOT` from `lionagi._paths` (line 16). It derives one path constant of its own from LIONAGI_HOME: `JOBS_DIR = LIONAGI_HOME / "mcp" / "jobs"` (line 23). It does not define a constant named `RUNS_DIR`. The name it uses is `RUNS_ROOT`, which `lionagi/_paths.py` line 21 defines as `LIONAGI_HOME / "runs"`. The question's `RUNS_DIR` name does not appear in the grep output, so I am treating `RUNS_ROOT` as the intended constant.

Caveat: I have not read `mcp/config.py` in full, and the grep was truncated, so a `RUNS_DIR` defined without the LIONAGI_HOME token is not ruled out.

When LIONAGI_HOME is not set, it defaults to ~/.lionagi (Path.home() / ".lionagi", then expanduser()). This is defined at line 20 of lionagi/_paths.py. (3) In lionagi/mcp/config.py, the two derived constants are RUNS_DIR = RUNS_ROOT (line 19), which resolves to ~/.lionagi/runs, and JOBS_DIR = LIONAGI_HOME / "mcp" / "jobs" (line 23), which resolves to ~/.lionagi/mcp/jobs.
